entities.name: Agostino Galamini
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Agostino Galamini (c. 1552–1639) was an Italian Dominican cardinal and Bishop of Recanati who served as Grand Inquisitor of the Roman Inquisition and as a confidant of Pope Gregory XV, playing a significant role in the most powerful Catholic ecclesiastical court of the early seventeenth century. Born in Cesena, he joined the Dominican order and became a prominent theologian before his elevation to the cardinalate in 1611.

As Grand Inquisitor, Galamini presided over the institution that investigated and prosecuted heresy, witchcraft, and theological deviance across Catholic Europe. The Roman Inquisition in his era handled cases from Spain to Italy to the New World, and its decisions had enormous consequences for individuals and communities accused of doctrinal error. Galamini's Dominican formation—the order that had historically staffed the Inquisition—made him a natural choice for this role.

He was also active in the conclave that elected Gregory XV in 1621 and enjoyed considerable influence at that pope's court. Gregory XV's pontificate was marked by significant institutional developments in the Church, including the formal foundation of the Congregation for the Propagation of the Faith. Galamini participated in this formative moment for Catholic global mission, and his Dominican intellectual formation shaped his contributions to both doctrinal enforcement and missionary expansion.
